name: AbbVie

points.text: Revenue is growing 10.3% year over year (strong).
Earnings jumped +2282% versus a year ago, but that mostly reflects a depressed prior year.
Operating margin is 36.6%.
Current ratio is 0.87, below 1 — short-term liabilities exceed liquid assets.
Free-cash-flow margin is 26.8% of revenue.
It trades at 18.1x forward earnings.
PEG ratio is 0.58 (price paid per unit of growth).
EV/EBITDA is 18.9x.
Free-cash-flow yield is 3.4%.
Price is 22.0% above its 200-day average: a strong uptrend, though stretched.
The 50-day average is above the 200-day average (bullish alignment).
RSI(14) is 57: neutral.
MACD is negative but improving.
It sits only 2.0% below its 52-week high.
26 Wall Street analysts rate it 1.7/5 on average (buy).
The average analyst price target implies 7.4% upside.
Over 6 months it returned +36.4% versus -1.7% for the MSCI World benchmark.
Last month: +2.7%.
Annualised volatility is 25%.
Worst peak-to-trough fall in the past year: 15.7%.
Beta of 0.19: defensive, moves less than the market.
No exposure to Healthcare yet — this would diversify the portfolio.

debate.said: Here is the case for owning AbbVie. Operating margin is 36.6%. Revenue is growing 10.3% year over year (strong). PEG ratio is 0.58 (price paid per unit of growth).
I'm not convinced. Current ratio is 0.87, below 1 — short-term liabilities exceed liquid assets. EV/EBITDA is 18.9x. MACD is negative but improving.
The cash generation covers it: free-cash-flow margin is 26.8% of revenue.

risk: Maximum position size: 18% of the portfolio (scaled for 25% volatility).
Every order costs a €1 fee, like on Trade Republic. Stop-loss rule: review at -15% from cost.
